brief: J.P. Morgan's Flows and Liquidity monitor makes three arguments. First, price-based financial conditions metrics tightened in 3Q26 because Global Agg yields rose nearly 15bp to just over 4.1%, taking the year-to-date rise to around 60bp, with high grade yields the largest contributor. Quantity-based metrics point the other way. US bank loan growth is stabilising just over 7% y/y, euro area loan growth is around 5%, August US high grade net issuance topped $90bn, and the US money supply proxy tracks around $1tr year-to-date to August 19th, which annualised could approach $2tr in 2026. JPM reads 2022 the same way, where quantity metrics matched the actual GDP softening better than price metrics, helped by a falling corporate net interest burden, so it concludes conditions remain supportive. Second, trading liquidity deteriorated mainly in cash USTs, near March 2026 lows, while S&P 500 futures, corporate bond ETFs and oil futures changed little, and Nikkei, gold and bitcoin futures stay historically illiquid, which JPM says amplified the debasement rally and its reversal. Third, positioning is long but not extreme: equities at the 70th percentile, bonds at 58%.
